You're looking for tendencies and maybe those guys up front, maybe they rely on their hand to tell them, hey, this is a pass set, and maybe that cadence that they kind of got a beat on. He timed it perfectly. Joe Brady starts his coaching career 5 and 0 on the road, the first head coach to do so since Jim Caldwell did it in 2009. I think um and a lot of those looks um where you're, you know, trying to make something happen and and uh getting out of the pocket. Got to do a good job making good decisions, making accurate throws. Daniel, what's it like to end the losing streak, but do it in a game where you said that you needed to be better? >> Uh, yeah. I mean, it feels good to win. I think um, you know, been in the league long enough to know that that winning is uh, you know, you got to celebrate the wins, enjoy the wins and and um, but yeah, certainly things to clean up and do better going forward. So, I know that um, and I'm I'll certainly be focused on that. >> You you know about the the 24-hour rule, but how quickly does that change when you have a Thursday game already? Yeah, I think, you know, speeds up a little bit for sure. Um, you know, starting getting into that stuff, uh, tonight and and early tomorrow morning. Um, so, you know, condensed week with Thursday night, you prep, you know, your prep's a little different, your practice week's a little bit different. So, um, you know, I think we'll have to turn the page quickly and and uh get ready for Houston. >> Daniel, for the last month or so, um, when Shane's come in here, we asked him just flat out, are you still a starting quarterback? he's defended you, but like as a player, does that weigh on you at all that it's pretty much a weekly question? >> Uh, I think I understand the way it works in in this league and and um the job and um all of it. You know, we're expected to play well week in and week out and and you've got to do that. That's your that's your job. That's my responsibility to the team. So, I understand um what happens when when I don't and and I've, you know, got to be better. >> You just comfortable with that? >> It was cool. It was a great feeling. You know, our team, we needed a spark in that moment and uh I was happy, you know, coaches gave me opportunity and Daniel found >> I heard Reggie right there just saying >> the last time you scored was like how much has he meant to you? >> He's meant a lot. You know, a guy who's played at a high level in this league, dominated, you know, played here. I'm just being in the room with him, asking him pointers here and there. Uh great coach, you know, high standard, too. So, it's just, you know, when you when your numbers call, you got to make the play. for you in particular, I mean, just the way this dynamic has changed in the receiver room. >> Yeah. >> How has that affected your role just as a leader and on the field? >> Um, that's a great question. Uh, I just same approach, but, um, I know guys are going to be leaning on me a lot more. You know, Ken leaving, Josh leaving, guys who've been in a, you know, pivotal role for the offense. Um, I know the coaches, staff, you know, younger guys, you know, I just try to lead by example. So, um, with the work ethic, with the with the grind, uh, coming out here making plays, and then on top of that, pouring energy into the guys, you know, let them, you know, let them know when the ball come their way, they got to make the play. >> Trey, I know this wasn't the best game necessarily for you guys, but it's still a wins and win. Just how big of a mindset change is that just to get that W for the first time in a while? >> Uh, it feels great. You know, we had a lot of distractions in the last couple weeks, you know, uh, fell short also. So, we just knew we had to come in and get a win by any means necessary and, um, this is something we can build on. It's a lot to clean up. You know, we'll get to the drawing board, watch the tape, and then get back to work. >> When you do something you haven't done in 5 years, do you reflect in that moment after scoring a touchdown of everything you've been through to get back? >> Uh, not necessarily. I know I know I could play. So, um, all the grind, all the every day working, you know, whether I was playing or not, I still had to put in the work. So, um, I was just so thankful that in that moment it it, you know, came about, you know. Um, honestly, whether you're playing on Sundays or not, you still got to put in the same work. So, um, when the ball find you and you get in the end zone, it's a special feeling. And, uh, we just try to try to live in that moment for what it is. >> I think it's more of just accumulation of reps. Uh, you know, we a lot of guys who don't have that much experience. So, the more time that we feel together, the more confident we play. And I think today you've seen flying around. A lot of guys are a lot more confident now. >> Having your big guys be able to bat down passes and, you know, be super versatile. What is that? You know, what does that what juice does that give you in the secondary? >> Oh, a lot. It makes our job a lot easier. It's like a racer. Like you can have a bad play to back the ball down. It's second down. So, it always good for us. >> Can you take us through the strip? It looked like he peeked back and saw you coming and you were still able to to get >> Yeah, he saw me and then he just turned and started running. I'm like, okay. Just keep chasing him then. But, I mean, it worked out well. So, >> they're talking about planning for the future, making moves for the future. You young guys are you're going to be a part of this future, right? I mean, is that what you is that what you're showing? >> Uh, I mean, we come in every day and our job is to do our best and put the best thing we can on film and we we have no control over what they do, but all we control what we what we do and what we can execute on the field. >> Justin, this is apologies, but just to get a win, how big is this for the locker room? >> It's always big to get a win. You know, it's what it's what we play for. We play to win every week, and when you don't win, it just make you want to win a lot more. So, we finally got another win. It feels good. >> How would you assess how the defense performed in particular today? Um, I watch the film to give you a real like a legit answer, but I think for the most part we did good. I mean, we won the game, so we did good enough to win, but as you watch film, I I bet there going to be a lot more things we can clean up. It won't be as good as it seemed right now, but right now, we just going to celebrate it. >> To see Tommy's touchdown, how cool was that? >> Oh, yeah. It's amazing. Especially as a guy like Tommy who works his butt off every day, but finally get a touchdown. It's great. >> There were a number of situations, penalties started to mount that gave Miami a number of first downs. How much of those things that you know you guys need to clean up moving forward as you go to a critical division game hostile environment on the road on Thursday night? >> Yeah, those penalties are small things. So, you know, small things when they add up can be uh >> very penalizing. But, you know, that's just one thing we have to just continue to hone in on the small things and and continue to stay one another and keep each other's head up. U cuz sometimes, you know, flags like that can get in your head. But, we just got to make sure that one, we don't let those things happen. uh two uh be ready to to have our brothers lean on us and continue to um push one another. >> The last few weeks it seems like you're just in the future and making it work for you. Does the feedback get to you? >> Yeah. Uh I'm just trying to go out there and uh do whatever the team needs me to do uh whenever I'm on the field trying to play my best and and make plays to help our defense and uh you know try to give us a chance to win. >> Some of the young guys made plays today. >> Justin and CJ. Is that kind of what you're building out of these young players? Yeah, I mean, uh, >> you're one of them. >> Yeah, I almost forgot the way you asked that question. U, but yeah, I think just us making plays out there, it gives us the confidence to that even though we may be young. Um, just going out there and playing football. Uh, same game we played when we were young, having fun, and enjoying it. Um, and there's no better way to do it, but on the the biggest stage. >> How do you explain the continuous nature of tips? I mean, it just seems like they came in punches and >> Yeah, really came a lot today. >> Yeah. Um, man, it it was I I just told uh Dang, where'd she go? I just told her that um I get it from Big Grove. Uh Grove Grove, I feel like Grove is always getting his hand on the footballs and and deflecting the passes. So, I was like, man, I need I need to join in on that. But, I mean, when when plays like that happen, um it's a big boost for the defense. And so, it's just any way to affect the quarterback. Um can't get to him, uh get his passing lanes and uh get hits on him. So, whatever way we can affect the quarterback, I'm willing to do. >> There's something else. how how CJ has grown. What's been that what's that been like to see? >> Oh man, amazing. Uh, you know, even though he's a young player, he acts like a vet. Um, he's very um he's always willing to learn and he's never um he's always coachable. He's always looking for um information that can help him be a great player and he's taking on the leadership role. Um he's a fun guy to have um back there and you know, I it's just great and and honor to see him grow into the player he's becoming. to see what Tommy's had the last couple of weeks. Signs the extension here, scores the touchdown. What was that moment like to see? >> Man, uh first we were just making sure he recovered the ball because he's used to stripping it out of the quarterback. So, it was I feel like it was a different [laughter] different uh moment for him, but I mean, he made the best of it. And shoot, just to see him get the get the touchdown, Wall-E get the sharp sack. Uh and it was amazing. Is there something else to like batting those passes down technique-wise other than just like stick your hand off and go hits it? >> Uh I mean we it credit to the times that we are practice those drills in practice. Uh um we try to make sure we do it in uh in practice. So you know when we doing the game it shows. So I think it's just something that you continuously work on and and uh yeah you you put so much time and effort into it that it it'll come up and show on on Sundays. Mondays or Thursdays? Yeah. How would you assess your performance today? >> Um, you know, most importantly, we got the job done and um, obviously a lot to improve on. So, that's the main thing I'm looking forward to is just, you know, getting we got short turnaround this week. So, you know, recovery starts now, the work starts now, and um, assess the film and, you know, look at how I could have been better. How how big has JT been for you just watching the way he works and goes about his business like just being a sponge when it comes to him? >> Yeah. No, that's that's the biggest blessing I could have asked for. Um I always knew that it was a phenomenal situation when I got drafted here and so um just mentioned it a couple of minutes ago. you know, JT's become like a big brother to me and, you know, he's he's obviously, you know, one of the greatest of all time and but at the same time such a humble guy and um you know, I couldn't have asked for a better vet and a friend in the room. >> Is there is there an issue with sharing carries like this as a running back? Sometimes you like to get into 18 to 20 carries. >> No, not at all. I think it's I think it's brought a spark. Um, I think we've been able to play off of each other very well. And um, when you have two different styles out there, it definitely keeps the defense on their toes and um, you know, I I I think it's keep keep kept both of us fresh and so um, no, I think it's been I think it's been a great thing and and our coach and you know, the entire staff has done a great job of managing that. >> It has worked out well, but did you initially wonder whether you would get some opportunities? I mean, there's jobs on the table, right? >> Yeah. Right. you know, and you at that what I would say today is you can just control what you can control and um you know, work as hard as you can and just focus on uh being great like and like I said, I got a great example of him of one of the greatest to do it. And that's that's what I aspire to be is of I've always aspired to be one of the best to ever play this game, if not the best. And so, um you know, just just keeping steady with the process and taking advantage of when when stuff comes to you and just kind of building that trust. >> You say Taylor's brought the best out he brings the best out of you. How do you bring out the good in him as well? >> Like I said, that's a testament to him because he's such a great student. You know, having all of the the success that he's had, you would think, you know, he's a a guy that kind of thinks he has it figured all out, but, you know, he's far from that. You know, we talk about we study all running backs uh game, you know, old, current, um you know, even college guys. And, you know, we're always, you know, he's a sponge himself still. And so, that's also been really inspiring to see. >> This rookie class is full of playmakers. You have CJ with the sack. How cool is it to see the guys that you came into this league with have success and have these big plays? >> Yeah. No, it's it's you know, it's a it's a big kudos to them and it's it gives me a ton of respect and a ton of hope for the the future and um like I said last week, I really appreciate the maturity of those guys and taking advantage of their opportunity and um you know, I think it's it's really good for us this season to start implementing our influence on the team and um how we can just help bring this team more success. big. I mean, we've been fighting for a win and feels good to get one. So, we're all happy and we're ready to, you know, take this and move on from it and, you know, grow from it. >> For you signing extension, get your first touchdown today. What was that moment like when you scored? >> Yeah, it felt great. I honestly didn't realize I scored a touchdown until everyone was celebrating. I'm like, "Oh, yeah, it's a touchdown." So, it felt good. >> What' you see on that play? >> Uh, so I seen I think it was Wall-E that hit him and then the ball was just loose and I was trying to make sure I recover the ball instead of like fumbling out of, you know, out of bounds. So, >> Tommy, when was the last time you scored That's a great question. Last time I scored a touchdown. >> The last time I remember scoring was in high school off of a block play. >> That's the last time I remember. Yeah. Important question. Where's the ball now? >> Where's the ball now? That's a great question. I don't know. >> Got track now. >> You're going to find it. Yeah. >> Where you going to put it once you do find it? >> Probably somewhere in my house. >> So, you you signed the extension. You've made a ton of big plays since then. Has that triggered anything in you or is it just business as usual? So, >> how would you assess how the defense performed today? >> Yeah, I mean, I think we made some good plays. We made some good strides. Is that easier said than done in a situation like that? >> I mean, it happens a lot. Like, we watch tape around the league. Guys are like all trying to get the ball. They're fumbling it out of bounds. So, that's all I was focused on. So, yeah, it's definitely, you know, harder than you would think. So, you got to really make sure you're, you know, focusing in that situation. >> Tommy, do you even have a 24-hour rule when you have a game on Thursday night? Uh, I mean, I'm definitely going to enjoy this. You know, it's hard to win and uh, definitely enjoy this one. But, you know, right back to work for sure tomorrow. >> There's been a lot of conversation about accountability in the defense and you guys have just continued to get better. What do you think was the switch that flipped this week, if any at all? >> Yeah, I think I mean, we've been just each week continuing to grow, continuing to get better and it's nice to see that come out, you know, as a win. >> How do you How have you seen CJ grow? >> I mean, he's been huge. I mean, he's been taking strides. It's great to see him make plays. that that sack was huge for us and I'm just, you know, proud of how he's continuing to grow and continue to get better. >> It was needed a lot. You know, it's been a lot that's transpired this year and it all it takes one. You can't stack wins and you can't say, "Oh, okay, we're rolling now until until you get one." And I think especially for the young guys, too, to go out there, play fast, play aggressive, make plays. It was really good for them as well. >> How have you seen Seth McGowan grow as a runner and a player and a person? Yeah, he's always watching and and evaluating not only myself, but like even when Quinton was here, Buck was here, he would watch the guys who he would want to be like and see their process. What do they do Monday through Friday to get ready for Sunday? And he continues to come back to the sideline and try to grab the iPad and say, "Oh, could I have done this?" Hey, look, you maximize every yard you could, but he's hungry and he really wants to figure out how to get better and how to keep taking his game to the next level. >> Does he remind himself of you? Does he remind you of him of of yourself? >> Yeah, definitely. When I came in, I was a sponge. I was like, "Hey, I'm not going to say too much, but I'm going to watch the guys who have done it for a long time at a high level and see what can I implement, and it may not work for me, but I'm going to try everything that they try to see if that can work in my plan as well." >> JT, there is a level of adjustment you have to make, right, when you're sharing the ball like this. Um, how have you adapted to it? And I don't know, do you like this arrangement or >> Yeah, I mean I still would I don't know how many carries I had, but it's all about being efficient. I think that's what I try to be whether it was two years ago when I first got into the league. It's like it's all about opportunities in this league. So what can you do with the opportunity that you have? Obviously, it's the greatest team sport. So you need all 10 other guys on the on the offense to to do their part to make a play successful. But what can you do to even help make other guys job easier so that you can be efficient? What do you think makes you two so efficient together in the back field? >> I think just understanding that every time we have an opportunity, hey, what are you seeing out there? And I'm also telling him, hey, this is what I'm seeing or remember on this scheme. Make sure this is where your eyes are at. So just going back and forth between each other and then also when we're running different schemes, maybe I didn't have a gap scheme yet, he had a gap scheme. Hey, how are they playing it? So when you can kind of have that communication back and forth, it goes a long way. >> What did you think of the defensive effort to help you all? Obviously you score this game. >> Listen, the defense was flying around. uh CJ was was playing like like a madman, but it it's complimentary football, but sometimes one side is going to have to do a little bit of the lifting and then that's where, you know, us as a offense, we got to make sure that, hey, we're doing our part because defense played their tails off today and we got to make sure that we help them as well each and every single week. >> Shuffling on your offensive line without Jaylen Travis, then you lose Bernard Ryman. How do you describe the job that those guys did up front for you today? >> They did a great job. I mean, and it's always tough when you got to make an adjustment like that in game. You know, normally if something happens and you know, hey, this guy's going to be out. You got all week to get reps together, communicate, >> but when it happens midame, it's like, hey, what what are the schemes we're going to now? What do you guys need? Like it it's definitely a lot of moving parts, but they did a great job of adjusting. >> When you're trying to focus on being efficient and get into a flow, what things do you have to change or do differently when you're not maybe getting uh as many carries in a row or as many as many carries in general in a game? >> You know, you really just have to stay patient. Yeah, you got to take what the defense gives you. I think that's one thing when you you feel as though you have to make the big play, but sometimes those big plays are the efficient plays. Hey, now instead of second and nine, it's second and four. So, it's all about being efficient to keep those chains moving. >> Trey scores that touchdown, first touchdown for him since 2021. How big was that and just what has he meant throughout this whole process of even the last few weeks? I was super excited because he's someone who who I've watched because if you talk to him and you listen and you hear about his journey and how he stayed consistent and how he stayed true to the process, he has a lot of knowledge. He's been a few places and for me to be able to to talk to him and understand like, hey, what does it take to win? What does it take to be a great player? Just because he's been so many places and I think when you have that experience and you've been in the league for a while is very, very good knowledge to have. >> You guys have had issues with threeand outs. uh what can you do earlier in drives to kind of set yourselves up to tonight? >> That's where the efficiency comes into play. You you want to stay on schedule. Anytime you get behind schedule, you get behind the sticks. Defense is able to do their thing and and they're able to kind of play at their will. So for us, it's like you got to be efficient on those first downs, those second downs because then it opens up the entire playbook. Everyone is comfortable. Everyone is like, "Okay, hey, what do I need to do to get these three yards, these four yards?" So, it's definitely about being efficient early because you never want to get behind

text: Amra, you just won in Germany in your home. How do you feel? >> I feel great, man. It's um it was a memorable three days. Um three days that I'll never forget in my career for sure. Uh my first game, you know, in Germany, a place that, you know, I call basically my second home. Um it was amazing from the start start of the game to the end. the way we played um as a team, the defense ball, just a collective effort, man. It was a I you know, being in Germany number one was was a blessing. It's been amazing. But being able to win like that um with the guys, with my teammates, in front of the fans here in Germany, it's been it's like a dream come true. >> Is there anybody who could stop you from scoring? >> It's funny you say that, Jay was just telling me there was no one going to stop you on that on that play. Um I don't I mean, I made a move. I caught it and I mean, it kind of opened up and I saw Jammo. Jmo put a huge block. Mahan's behind me. All the guys were were pushing for me to score. I'm like, I got to score this one. So, kept going and sure enough, got in. But that was um yeah, that was a that was a sick play. >> I loved your tunnel fit. Could you talk about the planning behind it, the message that you wanted to send, and just more broadly what you think about um tunnel fits? >> Yeah. Yeah. Um, so my mom, you know, she told me like 2 or 3 weeks ago, you got to wear the lid hosen. You got to do it. Like it's a it's a Bavarian thing. They do it out here. I'm like, where am I going to get it? I'm not just going to put on some, you know, Amazon laid out hosen. And so we, you know, talked to the lines. They actually got us all hooked up with some amazing laid out hosen that they found out here in Germany. They had the whole the whole get down, you know, the the jacket, the shirt, the boots, the socks. And so me, um, me, Isaac, and Hogan, we all got on board and did it. And I think it was I think it was awesome. I think you know we had fun with it and you're only in Germany so many times so why not? >> I mean we use the word great when we talk about the Lions and that's exactly how I would describe those two touchdowns. But what's the inspiration behind the second touchdown celebration? >> It's funny you asked that. Uh we had a uh we had a meeting I think it's our Saturday meeting. Uh Coach Kath comes up and he does his his presentation of you know rules that we have to be careful and be alert for. Um it's different stuff every week and he was showing us a NFL Europe game. Um it was situational. Something was going on and the guys scored and they did that celebration and we were all laughing in the in the in the meeting room and we're like we got to do that when we score. So I I said first touchdown we got to do it. I scored the first one. I was too too lit. I forgot to do it. So that was that. I get on the side. I tell Jir if you score you should hop on the hop on a little blue thing. It'll be sick. And just do that. And Jamir's like hey I'm going to do that. So J uh Jir scores. He does that. TLA blacked out too. He was, you know, lit his first touchdown of the year. And I'm like, I scored a second one. I was like, "Okay, now we got to do it." So I was on the ground when, you know, they pushed me in. I was on the ground. I was like, "Tlah, let's do the celebration. Let's do it right now." He's like, "All right, let's do it." I got down. We all did it. It was lit. >> Speaking of Jir, when you know, he had 250 touchdowns. [snorts] You had almost 100 yards, two touchdowns. When you guys, you know, you guys are superstars on this team. When you're superstars are playing at that kind of level, you guys, >> uh, I mean, yeah. I think, you know, we have a lot of good players on our team. I think I mean yeah when you're when you're when your players your good players play well um I think it's you ask any team any coach I think that's what I mean that wins you games obviously uh we got a lot of guys that can make plays whether it's me J Mo Leaporta Jir um Tislot today with a huge touchdown that he had um a lot of guys on offense with our old line I mean I feel like we can do so many things but um yeah it's been you know to have to have your guys play well I think that's the goal every week. Um, but whoever gets it, man, we're just proud to go out there and and put up points anyway. [snorts] Um yeah. it comes position. Yeah. Fore football. contact Alice. your teammates but first time in Germany for you it's like you're home. Um how was it for them? How was the feeling in the in the locker afterwards? What's what's the German [snorts] for them? Yeah, I think um from what my teammates have told me uh from just being out here, man, they they're loving it. They loved it. Um you know, some of my teammates have never left the country. Some have never been in Europe. So, for them to be out here, just being out here was, you know, was amazing. Uh some of them even told me, "Thank you, man. Thank you for I they're like, "Thank you for allowing us to be out here cuz I feel like without you, we wouldn't be here." So, um they've been very grateful. Um they had loved it out here. Obviously, after the game, they're excited because we won. Um, we played pretty good. So, the guys, man, I think the guys are going to have a good taste in their mouth from Germany, especially after the way we played. So, um, it's been an amazing trip. >> Couple more guys. >> Omro, you mentioned, you know, pregame that you felt it was your duty to help expand this game into Germany. You know, after a win like that, what do you you feel like you showed about the tenacity of the Detroit Lions and, you know, the son of God himself? >> Yeah. Um, I I feel like, you know, playing my first game here in Germany, um, in front of the fans was was amazing. I hope hopefully, you know, I think as a kid, like they can, you know, kids can finally watch the game because it's on at 3:30. Um, different timing than normally on Sundays. Um, but to gain any type of Lions fans, um, would be amazing. I know, you know, some kids when you're a kid, you get like a Lions ball or you have like a Lions jersey and you're four or five years old, you don't really know anything. But as you get older, like this is the first jersey I had. Now I'm a Lions fan, you know, 10 years later. So, um, to try to build that here, to try to build in more Lions fans, football fans in general. Um, and yeah, I think the way we played, I feel like, you know, Detroit, Detroit and German, I think Dan said it earlier in his presser. I feel like we do have, you know, some similarities in the grit and the way, you know, Detroit is built, the way Germany's built, um, the way people work, uh, their mindset, their work ethic. So, uh, yeah, like I said, it it was it's been amazing. Come on, bro. >> Obviously, you were juiced for the game, obviously. Do you feel like your teammates were for you as well with with all the production you guys had? >> It's a great question. I mean, I would like to think so. Um, I I don't know for sure. Uh, but I think we were juiced in general. I think that was one of the messages that, you know, Coach Campbell uh told us earlier in the week and even, you know, the day before is, you know, we're all traveling far. Sleep schedule's different, practice schedule's different, meetings, everything's a little different, but the team with the most juice is going to, you know, come out with the win. Everyone, um, gets paid a lot of money to do a lot of great things. Um, but I think if you bring the juice and play, you know, just play harder, I think it usually turns out pretty well. >> Talk to me about that offensive effort. Um but we'll continue with that same process this next week and um try to get it as healthy as possible as quickly as possible. >> Well, we just Yeah, I mean I I didn't feel like during the week of practice I was driving the ball the way I wanted to just cuz some of those deeper inut routes and the the ball's down the field and um you don't know until you get out there that adrenaline starts kicking a little bit and obviously it was good enough. And you referred to the pass to Josh play how you acquired that with him already. >> Yeah, I mean I think I like I I kind of said I think I need to do it even more. I it was early earlier in that game I didn't trust him on to win on a leverage. Um that wasn't a great leverage for him but he ended up winning on and you see on the tablet and you're like all right he won. Um, and so that then later in that drive, the next drive, I threw it to him on a trust a play like that. And then you get one-on-one and you you got to let your guys go out there and make plays. And so, um, he's here for a reason and it's to make those plays and so I got to trust him to go out there and make the play and and he proved that he can do it. >> There were a couple times where you went to get the football for guys with first touchdowns. What's the significance of that? >> Yeah, I mean, it's just such a I mean, playing in the NFL is a dream. Like, as a kid, it's a dream and you never know if you're ever going to get that first touchdown when you get here. And so, I still know exactly where my first touchdown football is. cuz I know how important it is to me whenever people come to the house and ask about it. And so I know when you you score, you're just celebrating. You know, you're just celebrating. You're not really paying attention to um what's going on. And so I just make sure to grab that so that they have that memory cuz they've worked their entire life to be here and they get to get in the end zone. Not a lot of people get to do that. And so they'll have that for the rest of their life. >> And where's your ball at? >> My I'm not going to tell exactly where it's at, but it's at my house. It's at my house and and pe and people have seen it. So they I don't want to tell exactly where it's at. How different did they look without Jesse? I mean, he was on the film, but there he was there. >> Yeah. I mean, it's it's hard to replace a player like that. I mean, I've played Jesse for a long time since he was in Cincinnati, and he is a he is a a true game changer. Uh X-actor there on the back end, and he gets guys lined up, he blitzes, he plays back, he punches the ball out, he does everything. And so, um obviously it's a good pickup for the Jags, but um they got they got a lot of compensation here, and they had other young guys stepping up and playing. Um, but it's hard to replace a guy uh like >> I think more than anything, it just proves that we can kind of attack down the field um like we believe that we can and defenses have have done a a job of kind of holding shell coverages and stuff like that, but if they're going to come down and try to stop the run, we have to prove that we can throw it down the field. And um it just showcases another level to our offense that we can continue to get better and better. And so, um, it's a it's a great confidence now. Uh, but NFL, you got to move on to the next week. So, we'll enjoy the plan ride home, move on, learn from the film, and, uh, try to be even better the next week. >> Okay. Thanks, Patrick. >> What do you make of the defensive performance? >> Um, we gave up a couple big passes that I wish we could have back, but overall, we kept them under 13 points and, you know, we kept the running back under 100 yards. So from that aspect, just got to watch film, see what we can get better at. It's something we can build off of. >> A lot of guys talk about the kind of juice and energy that brings it around. >> Absolutely. I mean, anytime a guy u make plays on this offense, it get us going. We want to see the offense score a lot of points. We love it when they put it in the end zone. So, anytime we see someone is bringing productivity to the offensive side of the ball, we get going. >> Are you on a set? >> You know what, man? You we just keep this momentum going, man. You know, um it's eight game stuff. It's opportunity to get us uh eight sacks. So, you know, week in and week out, we just get to the quarterback. How much? >> I mean, for us as a D line, I mean, we don't get to pick and choose when we finish. I mean, the team goal is the the big goal, the offensive line, the D line. And so, it's not like a on and off switch where we can go like we got to finish this, you know, we come in with the mentality always looking to finish, always looking to affect the game in a positive way. I mean, I never had doubt. Always a big believer in faith. Never had doubt that that storm would eventually pass. So, right now, it's about riding a storm and continue to prepare yourself week in and week out. >> Chris, the reports that you you travel on your own to get here. How did that uh factor into you and getting ready for the game? >> Uh it played no factor. Um it was a 30 minute commute from here to Mississippi, so >> a little bit of nothing. >> Okay. Thanks. Thank you, Chris.

title: Kansas City Chiefs vs. Atlanta Falcons - Official Postgame Show | Chiefs Rewind
text: Under pressure, SACKED AT THE 31-YARD LINE. DOWN, THROWS A WHEEL ON RIGHT SIDE. IT'S CAUGHT. TOUCHDOWN AT THE FAR FRONT PYLON. HERBERT IS ABSOLUTELY EATEN ALIVE. It's Drew Tranquill FAR, TOUCHDOWN. KEN WALKER III. And here comes a rush, and he's going TO GO DOWN. GEORGE KARLAFTIS. >> WELL, THAT WAS FUN. Mitch Holthus with you, Voice of the Chiefs, along with senior team reporter and director of editorial content Matt McMullen here. The Chiefs get a 35 to 13 win over the Atlanta Falcons. Kind of felt like I was in a time machine and went back to 2018 and 2019. >> Yeah, that was so much fun. But you know, the word that comes to mind for me that you might not think of when you look at the box score is resilience from our team. To not have K9 here in this game, to lose Travis Kelce for a good chunk of this game, to not have Trey Smith for much of this game, and to put on the offensive performance they did is pretty cool. >> It's a crazy 36 >> We'll get into that later in this episode. But, let's just start with Isiah Johnson. We're going to have Isiah here in just a little bit. Isiah Johnson was K 10 today or EJ 10. Very much like a Ken Walker kind of day. 171 all-purpose yards and two receiving touchdowns. >> Let's talk about some of those big plays. So, the opening drive, he has 36 rushing yards on just five carries before the 12 yd touchdown catch. On the drive before halftime, he hauls in a 34 yd screen that sets up Josh Downs touchdown. And the drive that really blew it open for us, a 6 yd touchdown catch. Isiah is so awesome. Like we love his attitude. I told you before the game like I'm not really even concerned. Like you want K 9 out there, but I believe in Isiah Johnson. Here's a crazy stat for you as well. So, a Chiefs running back has now topped 130 scrimmage yards seven times this season in just nine games. You want to guess how many we had from 2022 through 2025? Four in four seasons. Now we have seven of those in just nine games. Ken has five, EJ now has two. Pretty cool. >> And again, Ken Walker the third came in to work Friday, tight groin, took every precaution, ruled him out Saturday. That meant Isiah Johnson was it or Nate Carter who they signed off the practice squad. He was cut by these guys on August the 30th. That was your running back room in this game. >> And no problem. >> No problem. Isiah took care of business and so did Nate Carter. Also played on special teams. But, Patrick Mahomes also looked like 2018 and 2019 in this game. First of all, another game of at least two touchdowns and no interceptions. That's three games in a row. That's not happened since 2021. But, in this game, 348 yards, five touchdown passes, eight different receivers caught passes, and the vertical explosive game was back in this contest. >> You know, I saw the new Godzilla movie earlier this week and there's a part of that movie where pans in on Godzilla's eyes and you're like, oh no, Godzilla's about to mess everybody up here. That was Patrick Mahomes here today. I mean just incredible. The 39 yd touchdown to Cyrus Sullon, the 50 yd pass to Rashi Rice, the 43 yd touchdown to Andrew Armstrong. This was Patrick's 50th career game with three or more touchdown passes. That's the most in the NFL since 2018 and his seventh career game with five or more touchdown passes. It was awesome. >> And 300 yards passing 30 times. >> Uh-huh. >> The rest of the Chiefs quarterbacks, love them all, 29. But again, the vertical passing game, you alluded to it, but you got a back shoulder throw to Josh Downs for an 18-yard touchdown. You got a stutter and go to Cyrus Allen for his first NFL touchdown on a deep throw. Rashee Rice, 50-yarder. Andrew Armstrong gets his first touchdown on a 43 uh yard high point. There was stuff that was happening in this game that we haven't seen in a while, if at all, at least in maybe four or five years. >> A lot of fun and their route running today was awesome. And guys finishing plays. You think about the Denver game or the Seattle game. Why did we lose those games? Well, primarily because guys didn't finish plays. Our guys finished plays here today. That Andrew Armstrong touchdown was all just one two. The DB gave up and Andrew's like, I'm right here. I'm going to catch this touchdown. And that route by Josh Downs was awesome. We're going to see a lot more of that over the next several weeks, I think. >> Atlanta's got a good defensive front, very fast. And so Mike Caliendo had to come in after Trey Smith went into concussion protocol. Then Creed Humphrey got poked in the eye later in the fourth quarter. But the offensive line did enough. They did enough to allow Patrick to shoot it down field. And again, it was great to see it. >> Again, resilience from our team. It would be really easy to say, hey, we're losing all these players to injury. It's not our day. Even that part in the first half where we had like four straight possessions that ended with punts, nobody hung their head. They said we're going to be okay. And what a game from our guys overall. >> We're going to talk about the defense cuz they need uh some attention here, but we will do that later. Let's now get some reaction from the podium. >> All right. Um as far as injuries go, really Wiley, um looks like he fractured his ankle. So that's not that's not a good one. Trey uh is in the concussion protocol, so he's he uh we'll see where that goes. Uh Kels left for a bit with a calf. He's he's been battling this ankle, so it's all kind of part of it there. Got landed on in that first catch and twisted up a little bit. All in all uh a good win um against a talented football team. I think Kevin's done a nice job with these. He's had some injuries and they're battling through that. Um likewise for for our group. I thought uh the guys that came in stepped in and played uh whether it's the offensive line or running back position. I mean there were some some guys that stepped in and uh really helped us out uh today and uh for these young guys they're getting better. I mean we're one of the youngest teams in the league, man. They just they're getting better every week and it's good that coaches keep coaching them and you got to have a little bit of patience with them, but they're doing they're doing a heck of a job. Uh and Emmit getting himself over uh 100 yd there with with the help of the offensive line. I thought that that was great on on his part. Great effort there. Um we left him in there at the end so he could he could get that and uh he took care of business there. Uh Pat had a huge day on the offensive side here. Pat had a huge day. Five touchdowns and uh was slinging it. I mean really did some nice things there. Rice had a big day um with almost 100 yd and then Cyrus uh likewise had a nice double move for a touchdown. Um our new guy Downs uh it looks like there's a connection there, right? I mean they uh uh they worked well today and that's on two days of practice and so look forward to incorporating him maybe a little bit more into to the offense as we go along. Armstrong who nobody knows um who does a great job on special teams for us and also steps in and and rotates in as a receiver. Had a huge play there too with a touchdown. So and then defensively I thought we just shut him down. Spags had a phenomenal game plan um as EB did on the offensive side and I thought uh the players on the defense side, I mean, just shut them down. Our defensive front was dominant against a good offensive line. The back end was nice and tight back there making plays. Linebackers did a nice job. So um that's an explosive group. I mean, they they've got the running back that's one of the best in the National Football League. They've got a couple receivers there that are good as anybody, tight end that's as good as anybody. So to be able to put the hammer down on those guys uh um I thought just job well done. And um and then Harrison uh had his five uh five extra points and a field goal. Normally you don't take points off the board. So uh I did in that case. That shows you how much confidence I have in him. All right. In case you ask Fahey. >> Andy on uh Emmit in particular, you obviously already had faith in Zay, but how much more is that expanded after today? I mean, what what did he enable you guys to do >> Yeah. Yeah, so I look at the players. I mean, the players have confidence in them. And the players uh they're going to tell you the whole story. When when when a kid comes in and he's good, you know he's he's good. And then obviously he's he's doing the right things as far as protections go. So the cerebral part of the game, he's taking care of that part, knowing the plays and the direction of the plays and how to set the plays and all those things he he's got. And then he has that skill that goes with it. And he wants to be in there. He's a great kid that way. >> And you mentioned Dallas I I did see >> Now that that one throw in the for the touchdown before they have that that's a trust play. I mean, he put it up there and Pat made a great play. And Pat trusted him to throw that. Um so you see those kind of things. That's we can we can develop and work with that. >> With uh with Cyrus too, I I know you've been seeing >> Yeah. >> a little more here and there, but that that was a big step forward today. >> Yeah, that was a good one. That was a double move and he set the guy up set the guy up, did a nice job with it. Came out strong. Sometimes you can die coming out of that second move and and uh he he came out with speed and still gave Pat enough room that he could work on on the sideline as needed. So we got a good bite out of the corner. >> Andy was not focused spreading around the way that he was today. What does that open up for the coaching staff both for this game and for the rest of the season? >> You know, that's listen, that's been his career. He he he's a luxury to to have and to coach and he does a heck of a job spreading around using all of his receivers. He's not afraid to use any of them and uh um there you know, you don't see a lot of that um around the league, but he um he's a great player. >> You guys had a lead in the fourth quarter um trying to kill the clock. What's your level of trust? I know you you handed it off to a rookie um and you just hope that he, you know, protects the ball or like he was comfortable. >> Yeah, so the Falcons do a great job of knocking the ball out, punching the ball out. And they I mean, you look at the San Francisco game, San Francisco comes in and uh you know, the they have the four turnovers there, knocking the ball out um so we were aware of that and him more more so than any of us was aware of that. He saw it on tape and you know, keeping the ball high and tight becomes important. Covering it in traffic. He did all those little things if you're going to spin, keep it close to your body. All the little fundamental things I thought he did a nice job with. And we all have trusted that he he does that. He's a very coachable, smart kid. >> Andy, specific to that, I think it was a third and nine pass to Emmett. You kind of slowed down and just just took the ball in. Was that an example of just, you know, being mature enough to recognize situation? >> Yeah. Yeah. No, I definitely like a young Garrison Hurst, man. He was rolling out there, huh? Rolling, rolling, rolling. Um, he was uh I thought he did a nice job. He all the way around he did a good job. Garrison standing back here by one of the all-time great players, man. No, all-time greats, man. >> And whether injury things just that I think you would have mentioned more if there was more to him, but I guess it looked like Kree did get poked in the eye. >> Yeah, Kree got poked in the eye. Yes. Yeah. >> And he's okay? >> Yeah. Yeah. >> And uh Mansoor came out um >> He landed on his back and kind of up on that shoulder area. I think it scared him more than anything. He's going to be all right though, so. >> Okay. Thanks, coach. >> All right, good. Thank you. >> Hey, today you you distributed the ball so well. So many different guys got touchdowns. You got five of them. How did the offense flow today especially when you think about not having Kenneth? >> Yeah Yeah, I mean I thought guys stepped up, you know? And not having Kenneth and then obviously Travis getting hurt early in the game, there was kind of an adjustment period where we weren't kind of doing what we were supposed to do and then as the game went on, guys stepped up and made plays happen and so um we were able to get a lot of guys involved. Um, there were still missed opportunities out there um but it was good to see other guys step up and make plays especially against man coverage. >> Patrick, did you have a purposeful point today to give guys chances? I mean you threw some passes in the testing windows and threw the ball at certain times. >> Yeah, I mean you got to win versus man. I I think I got to be able to give him chances. I think there was times where I didn't give chances. I mean I'm thinking about early in the game I took a sack I think and I could have maybe thrown it to to Josh on the corner route. Um, and then some other times where I could have maybe gave guys chances versus that man coverage, but if they're going to play man we have to prove that we're going to beat it and guys did that today and so how can we build on that and and keep that going the rest of the season? >> Patrick, can you just sort of speak to what Emmett did for you guys today? I mean obviously you already had faith in Emmett. You spoke about him a lot. How did how did that play into the game today? >> Yeah, I mean he did a great job. You know, he he runs tough, he runs hard, he breaks tackles. Um and then whenever he gets chances in the receiving game, he catches the ball and makes plays there too as well. And so um I I'm I'm happy for him cuz he comes in with the right mindset every single day. I talk about it, he's a smile on his face. He he wants to be he wants to be great, he wants to contribute in any way possible. And obviously when having Kenneth and how great he's playing, he hasn't got as many opportunities, but when his number got called, he stepped in and made the plays happen. And so um that's going to be great to have as the season goes on and we get Kenneth back as that one two punch. >> And just just to that point too, I mean to have a guy like Kenneth be out and just be able to replace him that way, I mean that that has to be pretty confidence >> Yeah, for sure. I mean and and he's put in the work for that. Um I don't think anyone can replace Kenneth and the special ability he has running and catching the football, but to have someone that can do it in their own way and can make plays happen and break tackles um that that's the what you want on the team is guys to be able to step up and make plays. And so um it was late notice obviously with everything happening, but he was ready and prepared to go out there and have a great day. Yeah, you kind of got matched up one on one with the nickel and um that was kind of the play. Xavier did a great job of kind of running that post route, grabbing the corner and and kind of bringing the safety with him, getting two guys and before the corner could re re redirect back there, I gave him a chance to to make a play one on one and he made the play. And so um like you said, we haven't got a ton of reps and that's why I think there are sometimes you're going to see on tape where he was open and I didn't give him chances. Um but whenever you do it in the game, that's the best reps to get. And so I'll I'll be able to have that trust as the season goes on. >> something like to get Andrew one play >> Yeah, I mean those are the best cuz that man puts in the work every single day, man. And and for him, I mean training camp of him taking all the reps when guys were down and preparing himself and getting there and then obviously he didn't make the team with the number count, but got back to the practice squad, practiced hard, got called up, blocks his tail off every single every single time he's asked to. And then um to be go out there and make a big play in a big moment uh that that's what you want. You want guys that that truly care and will do it are selfless and will do whatever it takes. Um, they get their moment, they make the play. No, it's big. I mean, that's a really good corner, too. And so for him to be able to run a little double move and take a great release off the line of scrimmage and then meet us give him a chance. I mean, at that point it was just tough to give him a chance down the field and um that was a big play. We missed this barely early in the game um in a similar type um spot, but for him to come back, have the confidence to make the play later in the game uh it'll be big for him and his confidence moving forward. >> Patrick, you mentioned getting your receivers involved. As a quarterback, is that something that you will be forcing the game to say, okay, this guy made this play now I have to step up >> It It's hard for me to do it. Um, but I think Coach Reed and Coach Bamy do a great job of calling plays for each guy so that they're part of the progression. They know that the play is called for them and um you never know how to get the the games on the go, who's going to be open. I have to go through my progressions, get the ball to my hand. Um, but the co- coaches do a great job of making sure everybody knows they're involved by how we're calling plays. Um, and then the flow of the game um that's usually when the good things happen and that's kind of um what happened for the most part today. >> Patrick, I mean, it looked okay, but I just wondered how your elbow felt. >> Uh I mean, obviously it felt good enough. Uh I was a little nervous going into the game just because it was a little sore. Um, but uh we did a great job. Julie and the whole training staff did a great job all week of just trying to make it sure that I was in a great spot to go out there and compete. And I was able to do that today. I'm sure we'll we'll have some ice on it going back back home. Um, but we'll continue with that same process this next week and um try to get it as healthy as possible as quickly as possible. >> You said nervous going into the game. You mean recently as this morning you were >> Well, we just yeah, I mean, I I didn't feel like during the week of practice I was driving the ball the way I wanted to just cuz some of those deeper in cut routes and the di- the ball's down the field and um you don't know until you get out there that adrenaline starts to kick in a little bit and obviously it it was good enough. >> Patrick, Andy referred to the pass to Josh as a touchdown as a trust play. Can you just speak to how you sort of acquire that with them already? >> Yeah, I mean, I think I like I I kind of said I think I need to do it even more. I it was early in the earlier in that game I didn't trust him on to win on a leverage um that wasn't a great leverage for him, but he ended up winning on and you see on the tablet and you're like, all right, he won. Um and so that then later in that drive, the next drive, I threw it to him when I trust a play like that. And then you get one-on-one and you you got to let your guys go out there and make plays. And so um he's here for a reason and it's to make those plays. And so I got to trust him to go out there and make the play and and he proved that he can do it. >> There were a couple times where you went to get the football for guys with the first touchdowns. What's the significance of that? >> Yeah, I mean it's just such a I mean playing in the NFL is a dream. Like as a kid, it's a dream and you never know if you're ever going to get that first touchdown when you get here. And so I still know exactly where my first touchdown football is and I know how important it is to me whenever people come to the house and ask about it. And so I know when you you score, you're just celebrating, you know? You're just celebrating, you're not really paying attention to um what's going on. And so I just make sure to grab that so that they have that memory cuz they've worked their entire life to be here and they get to get in the end zone. Not a lot of people get to do that and so they'll have that for the rest of their life. >> And where's your ball at? >> My I'm not going to tell exactly where it's at, but it's at my house. It's at my house and and and people have seen it. So they they I don't want to tell exactly where it's at. >> How different are they looking without Jesse Bates? I mean he was on the film, but out there he wasn't there today. >> Yeah, I mean it's it's hard to replace a player like that. I mean I've played Jesse for a long time since he was in Cincinnati and he is a he is a a true game changer uh X factor there in the back end and he can get guys lined up, he blitzes, he plays back, he punches the ball out, he does everything. And so um obviously it's a good pickup for the Jags, but um they got they got a lot of compensation here and they had other young guys stepping up and playing. Um but it's hard to replace a guy like >> And what's this game plan being like this leader confidence more than last year in the season? >> I think more than anything it just proves that we can kind of attack down the field um like we believe that we can and defenses got have have done a a job of kind of holding shell coverages and stuff like that, but if they're going to come down and try to stop the run, we have to prove that we can throw it down the field and um it just showcases another level to our offense that we can continue to get better and better. And so um it's a it's a great confidence now. Um but NFL you got to move on to the next week. So we'll enjoy the plane ride home, move on, learn from the film and try to be even better than next >> Okay, thanks Patrick. >> Thank you. >> Thanks sir. >> The man of the hour here in Atlanta, the Chiefs won 35-13. I want your reaction when you found out K9's not going to go. You've been a great tag team partner with her and now you're going, whoops, it's your game. What was your reaction? >> Honestly, I just had the same approach to practice, but I knew that I was going to have a, you know, bigger load for the team. And just kind of just going out there and just doing what I've been doing every single day in practice and like I said before, whether if it's 20 carries or whatever it may be to help the team win, that's what I'm willing to do. So just trusting and believing in myself and doing that. >> But 171 yards in all purpose. It was on the ground for a hundo and you're receiving. Uh you've shown some great acumen as a receiver. What about getting it both done? >> Oh yeah, like I said, I don't want to be one dimensional as a running back. So just being a weapon out there and Pat does a great job of reading his check downs and and able to give me the ball in space. So shout out to him for that too. But just as a running back, I don't want to be just a one dimensional guy. I want to be out there and affect the game in different ways. >> Isiah Johnson again, the man of this game. All right, let's take the first touchdown. Little swing route. What about that play and how to develop? >> Yeah, honestly just getting out on my route and Pat making a good pass, but also just being in space, man. I don't like getting tackled in space. So I just wanted to go in there and score for us. Feel like that first drive was big for the momentum too as well. So just going down there and scoring right away was huge. >> What about staying patient cuz it got a little tough cuz we were just kind of grinding away. Couldn't get that second score. What about staying patient as an offense and you as a runner receiver? >> Yeah, that's how the game of football is. Sometimes, you know, it's going to be two, then it's going to be three, then it's just got to stay with it and then eventually, you know, it's going to break. So just being relentless through that whole process process and understanding that, you know, the next play is the most important play. Every play is not going to be a big gain, but just trusting it and just trusting the O-line up front and those guys too as well. >> Second touchdown, little chip and release action. What about that play and able to get it in space again? >> Yeah, just going through my progression, being able to help out in the chip game, give Pat time to throw and then slipping out free. I feel like they kind of fall asleep on that sometimes when I protect and then get out on my route. So just being, being available is what, is what, what I'm, I told Pat I'll be available for him. So. >> Arizona this week, you and I talked at Style Lounge on Thursday night. We're only nine, nine out of 17 here. As a rookie, we're just past the halfway mark. What about learning how to be a pro and training yourself to, because we now, it's, it's on. >> Yeah, like I said man, the NFL is a grind, but just taking it one day at a time, blocking out distractions and you know, the, the work throughout the week is what uh helps us have success on Sundays. So I think just continually grinding, uh that's what I've learned so much about the NFL is that you got to work every single day. You can't take days uh for granted. Um just doing that throughout the, the season will help me be successful and help this team be successful moving forward. >> Tobe was scrambling because you being >> Hello man. >> in the middle, you were off, did you miss special teams? >> Yeah, I did. I actually went to the meeting yesterday too because it was just hard not being there man, but uh Coach Tobe knows that I'm willing to do whatever it takes too. So um he has a lot of trust in me and those other guys did a great job today too. >> If you go for 171 every week, we'll figure out special teams. >> I'll still, I'll still do it though. You know me. I'm, I'm ready at all times. So. >> my gosh, what a joy it is to have this guy in the Chiefs Kingdom, Emma Johnson and a win today here in Atlanta. >> Yes sir. >> Chris, what do you make of the defensive performance today? >> Um we gave up a uh couple big passes that I wish we could have back. title: Klint Kubiak and Fernando Mendoza Postgame Presser | Week 10 vs. Seahawks
text: All right. Um, Brock Bowers has an ankle, so we'll, you know, reevaluate him tomorrow. Take any of your questions. >> Clint, in the first half, you were having some very good success rolling Fernando out and the second half you went away from it. Was that because of the Bowers injury or if not, can you talk about that please? >> No, should have should have done more of that for sure. >> Just in general, what do you make of Fernando's first start? >> Um, you know, he was he was well prepared. He had a he started the game really well and uh you know overall for his first start I thought it was a good start. >> What do you want him to take away from this experience against a defense and a team like Seattle? >> Uh there's there's a lot we'll watch the film together. Um we can learn a lot from from every part of this game, you know, but uh you know overall we have to play better. We got to support him better. I got to I got to help him better in second half. Credit to Seattle. >> Uh, coach, why were why was Seattle so effective on those DB blisses? They W got home like three times on Mendoza. >> Yeah, it was just uh, you know, they had good calls and um, credit to them. >> It it looked like you had a fiery message for the offensive line uh, on that first after that first drive out of the second half. Just what what was the message there? uh you know we just uh we expect more from ourselves coming out of that coming out of the tunnel in the third quarter and uh you know expect more out of myself as well. So um obviously the the the second half was was not good enough. You don't you don't give yourself a chance to win. I thought defensively took a step forward today. They kept us in the ball game and and we had to play complimentary football. >> Clint, you you talked about coming into this one you said you wanted to keep it simple for Fernando. Kind of keep it to what you guys have ran all practice. Did it feel like at times it was kind of a little too stagnant in terms of the game plan? >> Um, you know, I thought I thought uh overall when we lost Brock, you know, you definitely saw a big change in production. How much does that kind of benefit you guys kind of understanding that this offense has kind of struggled to do that all season long? Will >> you say it one more time? I was saying, how much does Fernando's ability to run the ball and more so his willingness to run the ball, how much does that kind of give you a little bit more to kind of chew on, understanding that this offense has struggled to do that all year long? >> Uh, yes, that helps. His mobility helps. It gives us a different dimension and Yeah. Yes. >> Any sense for how serious Brock's injury is at this point? >> There's not. No, it's just all I know is it's an ankle. Glenn, when you look at the overall performance from Fernando, how much do you zero in on his response to the big hit taking big hits? Sort of the the plays that didn't work or or the failed. So, you can zero in on the poise and the composure that he kept more so than the successful drives. >> Yeah, that's not a surprise. That's that's who he is. Um, you know, um, you know, that's that's why he is who he is. Obviously, he's he's an excellent player, but he's got poise, he's got maturity, he's got leadership, and that that showed, you know, all throughout the week. >> You you all have been able to protect the quarterback pretty well this year, but but six sacks today. Just what do you make of of not being able to keep him upright? >> Yeah. Well, I think I think there's a lot that goes into that. Number one, credit Seattle. They did a good job. Number two, um we have to be better helping our quarterback. And then number three, I think obviously you win a rookie quarterback, then there's chances to throw the ball away at times. And um there's there's a lot lot more than just one thing, but you're not going to win a game taking six sacks. >> Uh I know you do a lot with the offense, but could you gather what they were doing differently with JSN uh from the first half to the second half? >> I think I thought they made some great offset plays, so that was that was a that was a big part of it. >> Clint, um under three [clears throat] yards per carry uh today. What was the trouble with the run game and and how do you go back to the drawing board to try to get that fixed? >> Um, you know, it was a positive first half. You have to sustain it for four quarters. Weren't able to do that. Got to come out of the tunnel, run the ball at first first call the second half is a is a, you know, run and we take a loss, but uh, I put it on myself. There's no one else to blame but me. >> It didn't seem like there were a whole ton of opportunities to to throw the ball and take deep shots today. Was that a matter of the the pressure or what do you make of not really being able to stretch the field? >> You know, I think uh that's what that's what this defense makes them so great. They take away uh they play, you know, complex shell coverage and take away the deep ball and they did that today. >> Guys, good. Thanks. >> Thanks. >> Thank you. >> Good afternoon, guys. >> Fernando, for you, you just assessing your first start. Are you able to just accept maybe just a rookie and and learning from it or to you is it only win or lose? >> I believe that it is more of a win or lose mentality. Coach Kubak holds us to a very high standard and that's what it comes down to at the end of the at the end of the day and there's a lot of things that I need to improve on that field. I'm excited to watch the film and get back to work. Fernando, um, after the Heisman, your mom said what she appreciated about you is you turn obstacles into opportunities. How do you look at today through the same lens in your first NFL start? >> Yeah, the Seahawks have a fantastic defense. We've seen it all season. So, a lot of credit to them and coach McDonald and fantastic. I mean, he's he's a special human being on and off the field. However, Coach Kubak always preaches and everybody doing their job. So, the next guy up I have as much confidence in. None of Nobody wants to play bad. Nobody wants to uh not play good. Just doesn't swing your way sometimes. >> Anything else for Jordan? >> Appreciate it. Thank you, [clears throat] sir. Teller, what made getting into a rhythm today so difficult? >> Um, it was a lack of execution in some of those critical moments for us as players. We were getting everything that we wanted. So felt like we were seeing it fine and you know you can't come out of that half and the first half with a was with no points. There was just lack of of details there on us. So um it was we knew it was going to continue to to work for us if we just kind of kept that same mindset and we had we had to get our we had to get ourselves going man and it was it was kind of on us as players from that standpoint and um you know credit to the defense for they played their butts off the entire game and um we had a chance there at the end. >> What happened on that uh exchange with Audric on the fumble? Uh it was just you know classic trying to pull it got stuck and uh can't can't happen though. Um especially on the exchange there. Um just got to make sure en sure we secure the ball no matter what happens and um that's on me. Exchange point quarterback's got to secure it so um won't happen again. >> What were they doing to kind of limit Chris today? >> Um yeah they're rolling to him the you know all day. you know, it was going to be expected with some of the stuff they were doing, but we still had opportunities and I got to find um those one-on-one match ups with him and and give him the ball. How much of a a difference did it make having Jordan out there for a lot more snaps and being able to get him the ball while they were covering up Chris so much? >> Yeah, I mean you see the you see the difference when it when you can be balanced like that and having both, you know, really elite targets on the outside and including Jawan and Vila and and and all of our guys. So, um we got the right p the right pieces in play and we got to find a way to execute better in some of those um you know short yard situations to get us in get us in those manageable situations. So again, it's uh sucks, but um I think more than anything, we understand what we need to do and get our best ball, get our best players the ball and and execute in those key moments. We had those moments where we could have we couldn't have got we could have got it done. >> What was it like having Travis back? >> Uh, it it was awesome. I think there was a couple plays that it should have been TFLS and he he creates four or five yards out of it. Um he's got this incredible feel. Um he's really good in cross pro. So having him, you know, Estim and Kamar all, you know, kind of interchangeable back there. Um it really helps us out offensively just from I mean every standpoint. So having to get him back and like I said, we got some pieces back. You know, we got some guys banged up too. So but it's the name of the game. Um and we got to go out there and execute it. So that's on us. It's just one game, but with with chance to be in first place or does it feel like a missed opportunity to kind of come out of this without >> Yeah, man. It feels awful. It is a missed opportunity. We we got to beat we got to beat those guys. Um you know, they I mean that's that wasn't a win, you know, by them. I feel like they're obviously a good team, but we feel like we lost that game as as the Saints. You know, we had opportunities there when we had those moments. So, um, there's going to be weeks, um, and sometimes you're going to lose a game and they had to, you know, teams are going to beat you, but I feel like we we shot ourselves in the foot there and that stings even more. So, um, I got to look in the mirror and and figure out how I can play better on certain plays to get us in those positions. Um, but still keep the same mindset. Um, and nothing's going to change from there. >> Kell seemed really, I don't know, he was not snippy, but he was short today. I mean, could you all sense that from him afterwards? Yeah, he was very he was upset. Um, you know, rightfully so. I think he as players, we failed him as as a coach. I think we had those moments. I we had a couple third downs where um I could have found Chris or I could have maybe made a play there. Um so we had we had those opportunities and he's obviously frustrated and we got to we got to find a way to win that game. So came down the wire. Um a lot of those games are going to be like that. So um but man, it doesn't have to be close. We got to we got to execute earlier on and um you know we're all we're all going to be upset and and um nothing's going to change. We got we got to prepare. You know, nothing's going to change from, you know, our mindset, but we got have to to kick into that next groove cuz um nobody else cares in the NFL. You got to do your job. >> I know Chris was the first read on that interception. Was that a play where fourth and one got to have it like you're just going to him or >> Yeah, I mean it was just a good play by DB. It's just um a tip tip ball. So, uh, we got everything we wanted there. It was just a good play. Um, thrown that 100 times out of 100 and, um, we got to find a way to to get that one and, um, that's just a football play that happens. So, it was a good kind of tip up to the guy and they made a good play. So, things like that happen, the fumble, those can't happen. So, um, got to ensure we get those and, um, just keep going. >> Figure coming in today that that Jordan was going to end up being featured or is that just kind of the way the game the game unfolded with the way they were defending Chris? Yeah, just kind of how it unfolded for sure. You obviously, you know, you want to have multiple weapons and um they did a good job of taking away him on some of those. Um but we still had opportunities all over the field and and Jordan did a really good job just kind of every single week he's continued to grow. I think earlier on, you know, we had a couple miscommunications. I'm still trying to get um a feel for uh body language and stuff like that, but I think we were able to kind of just keep at it and connect on some of those passes. Thank you. >> All right, we just heard from quarterback Tyler Shuck and Scott, we were just talking about this. Essentially, three new guys and the replacement right now of Eric McCoy who's at center. We talked about just how significant that is as well. When you look at the impact that Eric McCoy has on this offense, what does it mean to have a loss at this point the season of him? >> Eric's a huge loss. And I I think anytime Eric goes down, he's been one of the hardest guys to replace on this team. And you go back to a couple years ago, people remember they start saying Saints started the season off 2 and 0. They were beating Philadelphia at home. Eric goes out and that kind of changed the course of that season early on. He's just when you lose a center with with the ability that Eric McCoy has in the run and pass game. That's really second nature compared to what he brings to you verbally and football intelligence wise cuz as a center you're relaying calls. You're telling which way you're sliding protection. You're doing all those different things in the middle of your guys. You got two guys over here, two guys over here that you're responsible for. So Eric's been one of the best in the business for a long time. And credit to Caesar Ruiz. Caesar coming out of college was he was really kind of a center coming into the league. He played guard because Eric was such a really good center. But it's an opportunity for Caesar to kind of show the NFL that, you know, this is kind of my natural position. And I thought Caesar did a pretty good job filling in for Eric >> Yeah. Caesar said earlier in the week that going back to the center position was like riding a bike for him, as you mentioned, something that he was already familiar with, but again, an adjustment at this point in the season. We're talking about adjustments, kind of alluding back to Tyler as well. How much of an adjustment is that for him to have to figure that out during the course of the game? Yeah, there's Listen, it kind of goes I didn't answer your question before about how much responsibility there is kind of on Tyler when he goes out of the game when when the center goes out of the game, but there's a lot on Tyler's shoulders. Alvin Chamra being able to get two touchdowns on the day. Scoring two touchdowns today. If you look at the box score, it doesn't really tell the story of of it kind of turned back time down here on the second touchdown. Alvin Chimera out of the back field is like taking candy from a baby. I think Alvin can be 15 years in the league and still be able to route up a linebacker. So continue to do those things with 41 because there is still is a space for him in this offense if you utilize him that way. So I it brought brought a smile to my face seeing him route up the linebacker down here because one I wasn't on the field getting routed up and he scored the touchdown for the Saints. But um I think Alvin's been one of the best out of the backfield at running routes. >> How consistent has he been and what part of that consistency that he brings into every game just kind of puts some ease like you mentioned on a quarterback who needs some assistance in certain areas? Yeah, you need plays like that because this game is a matchup game. It's about getting guys on other guys that that aren't as good athletically and that you feel like you can isolate and to isolate him on a linebacker in the red zone. That's a high percentage plays and that's really what you're doing throughout the game as an offensive play callers calculating you want the odds in your favor that your matchup is going to win. And I think it's great to see that you have a running back in Alvin who can still do those things. want to mention uh Travis Hen being able to come in as well, getting taken off of IR, being able to see some reps from him that we haven't seen since the beginning of the season, also being able to play against his brother, which is a unique experience. Do you think this one maybe hurt a little bit in terms of just how it all played out? >> I'm sure, especially with Thanksgiving coming up, there'll be a little bit of bragging rights. Yeah, there'll be bragging rights for sure. um especially taking the now they take the lead in the NFC South. But it was good to see him get out here again today because you know coming off an injury just like we talked about with Jordan it's all about building confidence getting through a game that's like a little milestone for you as a player after you're injured and he got through this game. Now he didn't unfortunately for him he didn't have enough opportunities and some of those opportunities comes down because you were you were not successful on third down. You know you weren't successful on third down enough to keep your offense on the field so that we could see uh Han get more of those carries and I think in the coming weeks he'll be a big part of this offense. Well, we're going to take a look at our our next games in just a second here. Uh, but want to first highlight what the defense was also capable of doing today.
