He's now at eight and a half sacks. He's leading the team, tying a careerhigh for him as well. I talked about a constant within Alvin Chimera. When you have a Grando who has been a constant as well, what can you rely on him for for a defense? >> He's just he's he's an athletic guy with with great measurables and body length. And he you see him and he's out there on the edge. He's fast enough to get around tackles, but he's also athletic enough to get that dip and that lean that you don't usually find in guys with that body type. And when he's not getting to the quarterback, he does a great job with that length of getting his arm and his hand up in the air and get into passing lanes. And I think even when he wasn't getting sacks or getting those box score type things, he was affecting the game by by his ability to get in Bryce Young's face today. >> Yeah. Well, you'll certainly need him moving forward. We're going to take a look at the next three games, though, because it's going to be a battle with the Midwest, if you will. And it doesn't necessarily get any easier from here, Scott. You have Chicago at Chicago, then you have to play the Bengals at Cincinnati, then back at home with the Packers. But this is something that we talked about. It's the weather part of it. You've been playing in the dome. It's nice and toasty here. As somebody who's from Chicago, I understand how chilly it could be at Soldier Field. You said those are the coldest games that you have ever played. How much is weather going to play a factor in the next ones? >> It'll be a factor. I think two coldest games I ever played and bar none is Chicago Bears. I can still feel the bone chilling cold. So, it'll be interesting to see what the weather's like. But, I think that's where defense always travels no matter matter of the weather. If you can get a little bit of a running game going, that'll help as well. And I think those are those are three opponents where I think a lot of people after a loss today, fans, you look at that like, oh, that's but as a competitor, as a player, when you lose a game like this, you want to go, you want to play the best. And that's why you're at this stage. That's why you're playing at this stage cuz you want to compete against the best. So, three opportunities and it starts with one of the NFC favorites. Chicago Bears, they've been playing as good of football as anybody. If you're a rusher, I want to sack Caleb Williams. I want to intercept Caleb Williams DB. So, that's the competitive firing you. you're going to listen all week about how good the Bears are and how you shouldn't have any chance and I think that'll give you an edge going into this game. >> Just a quick point of that as well because that's a big factor. Caleb Williams has mentioned that he is going to throw the ball no matter how many interceptions that he throws for. But how much of an opportunity is that for a Saints defense against him? >> Yeah. And I think the message throughout the defensive meeting room this week will be I think back to when we played guys like Brett Favre. These guys are gunslingers and they're going to throw it no matter what they're and that's what makes them great, but it also can be their Achilles heel a little bit. And when they do throw it up to you, they're going to make some plays by being a gunslinger, but they're also going to make some mistakes. And when they make that mistake and they throw you that ball right in your chest or right in your hands, you got to make them pay for it. And that's how you get your advantage against quarterbacks who like to just gunsling mentality like that. >> Well, Scott, like you mentioned, a lot of opportunity ahead for the Saints. They'll be traveling to Chicago for the next one, and you'll be able to see us in studio for the next one as well. As always, thank you so much for watching the Saints postgame show. for Scott Shanley. I'm Clea Butler and we will see you all next week. >> Shot is called a play. 122. Ronnie Bell with a one-handed catch and a touchdown in the back left corner. Ronnie Bell. Welcome to the New Orleans Saints. What a catch. Saints bring some pressure and he's going to go down.

title: How 49ers Insider Grant Cohn Botched the Trip to Dallas
text: I thought I was gonna go to Dallas. Turns out all the beat writers got there. Eric Branch, I heard him. Vic Tafer, Nick Wagner, Lombardi, although he doesn't really count as a beatw writer. He's more of a designated embracer. Harrison Rich, Jennifer Lee Chan, all of them made it. I didn't. Why didn't I make it? Okay, first off, I think there was some bad luck involved. Like one, I booked my flight for 3:30 because there h I booked this like a month ago. There happened to be a non-stop out of Oakland to Dallas on Southwest. I'm usually a United guy because United has great customer service. They're a little more expensive, but Oak I'm I live in Oakland and Oakland is a Southwest hub. I've had some terrible experiences with Southwest, but I was like, you know what? I can't pass this up. It's a good price. It's 20 minutes from my house. I'll just cruise down. Bada bing, bada boom, I'm in Dallas. As I'm going down Hegenburg in the in the Uber, I see the news. National ground stop. I don't know what it means. It doesn't sound good, but I'm I'm optimistic and I'm also in denial. I'm not really in reality and I'm thinking it's going to work out. God won't let me not get to it's going to work out. I don't need to take this seriously. In hindsight, it would have been nice to leave earlier in the day. It wouldn't have been I would have made it if I had left earlier in the day. I would have made it probably if I had left out of San Francisco, but why? How? I didn't know this was going to happen. So, I get to Oakland airport. Plenty of time. Um, no one knows what to do at the Southwest counter. I just need to like drop off my bag cuz I I'm packed for Mexico. I was The plan was to go from Dallas straight to Mexico. So, I have this huge bag. I'm trying to drop it off. They're not taking bags. They're like, "Look, uh, they just we're not flying." And so we're not taking So you just stand there or go home. So I'm like, "All right, I don't know what to do at this point. Had I done it again, I would go online and book another flight. Just start spending money wildly. Hundreds of dollars. Just buy more tickets. I could have bought a ticket at 2:00 probably somewhere that left on Saturday out of San Francisco. I it seemed like the move was to quickly get a United flight from San Francisco to Houston. Nick Wagner figured this out. He's the savviest of the travelers on the beat. I don't know how he's good. title: Instant Analysis of the 49ers' 46-40 Win Over the Dallas Cowboys
text: That game was way too close and that ending was very interesting. The 49ers just beat the Dallas Cowboys 46 to 40 and the Niners almost gave it away right at the end. Kaylin Black fumbled and then fell on top of the ball and the Niners put the game away. That's how close it was against the Dallas Cowboys. No one thought it was going to come down to the end. They thought it was going to be We thought it was going to be a blowout and it really should have been because the Niners offense was incredible. Niners defense, another story we'll get to them in a little bit. The Niners off, let's start with Brock Pury. was playing like Superman and he had to play like Superman because with the exception of Keenan Allen, his wide receivers weren't getting open. Talk about Christian McCaffrey in a minute. But Brock got sacked four times in the first half, five times total. Also had another one that was called back because of a defensive holding penalty. Was running for his life, playing like Superman. Playing great, extending plays, getting out of the pocket at will. And when he gets out of outside the pocket, you're freaking dead. Uh he's top three quarterback in the league right now along with Josh Allen and Patrick Mahomes. Maybe you put Joe Burrow there right as well. Caleb Williams, but I have no more questions about Brock Perie. He's absolutely elite and he makes plays that only a handful of other guys can make. I don't care what size he is or how how strong his arm is. I mean, that play he made where he uh scrambled to his right and then hit Christian McCaffrey for the long touch. I mean, how many guys can actually physically make that play? Allan Mahomes, him, Caleb Williams, not Joe Burrow, not Tom Brady. It was funny listening to Tom Brady have to begrudgingly praise Brock Pury for all these things that Tom never could have done. Kyle Shanahan was struggling though. The running game wasn't working. the the the p the offensive line was getting worked. Kyle had to join the party. He was a one-point lead at halftime um because the Cowboys missed a field uh extra point. All of a sudden, Kyle finds some confidence in Caleb Black. He trucks Caleb DS, scores a touchdown. That felt like it should have been the game right there cuz now you got a running game. They rush for more than 200 yards. Uh Brock Pur didn't have to do that much, but he was freaking amazing. But the defense was awful. The defense does nothing well right now. Gave up 40 points. Nick Bosa, three offside penalties. I mean, they had one sack. It was charity. Dak Prescott ran out of bounds for no gain. And that uh Dre Green was recorded was credited for the sack, but he didn't touch them.
